Subject: Proposed Mar 31 narrow-window: private runtime refresh & escape-route

Jordan / ACME ops,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier — following up with a compact plan for the Private runtime refresh (minor version bump and kernel/security patches) we discussed. We want to keep the window as short as possible and preserve your pinned version option until we’ve verified stability. High-level: the change will touch the inference runtime and network control plane components in your VPC deployment (no data plane migration).

Proposed window
- Date: Wed Mar 31
- UTC window: 02:00–03:30 UTC (local: Tue 03/30 19:00–20:30 PT)
- Expected interruption: targeted canary slice only; full-fleet outage only on explicit abort.

What we’ll do (summary)
- Pin existing model runtime to v1.14.2 for production slice during preflight.
- Apply runtime binary patch v1.15.0 to canaries (10% traffic).
- Network prep: BGP quiesce for canary subnets, apply ACL delta for health probes; no CIDR reassignments.
- KV cache eviction handshake and warmup to avoid cold-start spike.
- Telemetry gating: metrics + error-rate lookback; automatic rollback if 5xx spike > 0.8% sustained for 5 minutes.

Rollbacks / escape criteria (short)
- Automatic rollback: latency P95 > 2.0s for 5 consecutive minutes on canary; or error-rate threshold above.
- Manual rollback: if we see persistent dataplane errors or network blackhole; will execute fleet-shelve (shelve API) and repin to previously pinned runtime.

Attachments: private-refresh-change-plan.pdf (full sequence), preflight-checklist.xlsx, runbook-canary.md

Next steps
- Please confirm the window by EOD Mon Mar 29 and indicate if there are blackout constraints.
- If approved, we’ll schedule a 30-minute preflight call 1 hour before the window and post a status update to the shared Slack channel (#acme-private-refresh).

Thanks,
Naomi

Jordan — quick technical notes to address your requests and document rollback timing. Adding this inline so the runbook and checklist can be updated accordingly.

Rollback RTO and steps (worst-case estimate)- Full-fleet manual rollback (shelve + repin + warmup): ~20–35 minutes. This assumes no cross-VPC networking issues and that the previously pinned image is available in the local image cache. If image cache misses occur, add 12–18 minutes depending on inter-region bandwidth.
- Canary automatic rollback: automatic serve switch to pinned runtime within 90–120 seconds upon meeting the rollback metric thresholds (we do an immediate KV cache invalidation then restart the canary process).

SOC2 / audit hooks- We will add explicit log markers to the control-plane logging stream for: BGP quiesce start/end, ACL delta apply, KV eviction start/end, canary promote/demote, and full-fleet repin trigger. Those markers will include ISO timestamps and request ids and persist to the audit log bucket for 365 days per the agreement.

KMS keys- Confirmed: we will not rotate or change customer-managed KMS keys during this operation. Key usage will be read-only and unchanged.

Network operational checklist summary- Preflight (T-60m): verify route advertisements, validate BGP neighbors, snapshot routing tables.
- T-15m: enable canary traffic split (10%), baseline collection for 15m.
- T+0: apply runtime patch to canaries, run warmups, validate error rates.
- T+30m: if stable, ramp to 30% for 20 minutes, then consider 100% if all signals green.

Attachments: runbook-canary.md (will be updated with the audit hook lines), preflight-checklist.xlsx (timelines + contact list).

Karthik
